In [[symplectic geometry]], a branch of [[mathematics]], '''Weinstein's neighbourhood theorem''' refers to a few distinct but related theorems, involving the [[Neighbourhood (mathematics)|neighbourhoods]] of [[Submanifold|submanifolds]] in [[Symplectic manifold|symplectic manifolds]] and generalising the classical [[Darboux's theorem]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last=Cannas Silva |first=Ana |url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-540-45330-7 |title=Lectures on Symplectic Geometry |publisher=[[Springer Science+Business Media|Springer]] |year=2008 |isbn=978-3-540-42195-5 |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-3-540-45330-7 |author-link=Ana Cannas da Silva}}</ref> They were proved by [[Alan Weinstein]] in 1971.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last=Weinstein |first=Alan |author-link=Alan Weinstein |date=1971-06-01 |title=Symplectic manifolds and their lagrangian submanifolds |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/000187087190020X |journal=[[Advances in Mathematics]] |language=en |volume=6 |issue=3 |pages=329–346 |doi=10.1016/0001-8708(71)90020-X |issn=0001-8708 |doi-access=free|url-access=subscription }}</ref> 

== Darboux-Moser-Weinstein theorem ==
This statement is a direct generalisation of [[Darboux's theorem]], which is recovered by taking a point as <math>X</math>.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><blockquote>Let <math>M</math> be a [[Differentiable manifold|smooth manifold]] of dimension <math>2n</math>, and <math>\omega_1</math> and <math>\omega_2</math> two [[Symplectic manifold|symplectic forms]] on <math>M</math>. Consider a [[Compact space|compact]] submanifold <math>i: X \hookrightarrow M</math> such that <math>i^* \omega_1 = i^* \omega_2</math>. Then there exist

* two open [[Neighbourhood (mathematics)|neighbourhoods]] <math>U_1</math> and <math>U_2</math> of <math>X</math> in <math>M</math>;
* a [[diffeomorphism]] <math>f: U_1 \to U_2</math>;

such that <math>f^* \omega_2 = \omega_1</math> and <math>f |_X = \mathrm{id}_X</math>.</blockquote>Its proof employs [[Moser's trick]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Moser |first=Jürgen |author-link=Jürgen Moser |date=1965 |title=On the volume elements on a manifold |url=https://www.ams.org/tran/1965-120-02/S0002-9947-1965-0182927-5/ |journal=[[Transactions of the American Mathematical Society]] |language=en |volume=120 |issue=2 |pages=286–294 |doi=10.1090/S0002-9947-1965-0182927-5 |issn=0002-9947 |doi-access=free|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=McDuff |first=Dusa |url=https://academic.oup.com/book/43512 |title=Introduction to Symplectic Topology |last2=Salamon |first2=Dietmar |date=2017-06-22 |publisher=[[Oxford University Press]] |isbn=978-0-19-879489-9 |volume=1 |language=en |doi=10.1093/oso/9780198794899.001.0001 |author-link=Dusa McDuff |author-link2=Dietmar Salamon}}</ref>

=== Generalisation: equivariant Darboux theorem ===
The statement (and the proof) of Darboux-Moser-Weinstein theorem can be generalised in presence of a symplectic action of a Lie group.<ref name=":1" /><blockquote>Let <math>M</math> be a [[Differentiable manifold|smooth manifold]] of dimension <math>2n</math>, and <math>\omega_1</math> and <math>\omega_2</math> two symplectic forms on <math>M</math>. Let also <math>G</math> be a compact [[Lie group]] [[Lie group action|acting]] on <math>M</math> and leaving both <math>\omega_1</math> and <math>\omega_2</math> invariant. Consider a [[Compact space|compact]] and <math>G</math>-invariant submanifold <math>i: X \hookrightarrow M</math> such that <math>i^* \omega_1 = i^* \omega_2</math>. Then there exist
* two open <math>G</math>-invariant [[Neighbourhood (mathematics)|neighbourhoods]] <math>U_1</math> and <math>U_2</math> of <math>X</math> in <math>M</math>;
* a <math>G</math>-equivariant [[diffeomorphism]] <math>f: U_1 \to U_2</math>;

such that <math>f^* \omega_2 = \omega_1</math> and <math>f |_X = \mathrm{id}_X</math>.</blockquote>In particular, taking again <math>X</math> as a point, one obtains an equivariant version of the classical Darboux theorem. 

== Weinstein's Lagrangian neighbourhood theorem ==
<blockquote>Let <math>M</math> be a [[Differentiable manifold|smooth manifold]] of dimension <math>2n</math>, and <math>\omega_1</math> and <math>\omega_2</math> two [[Symplectic manifold|symplectic forms]] on <math>M</math>. Consider a [[Compact space|compact]] submanifold <math>i: L \hookrightarrow M</math> of dimension <math>n</math> which is a [[Lagrangian submanifold]] of both <math>(M,\omega_1)</math> and <math>(M, \omega_2)</math>, i.e. <math>i^* \omega_1 = i^* \omega_2 = 0</math>. Then there exist

* two open [[Neighbourhood (mathematics)|neighbourhoods]] <math>U_1</math> and <math>U_2</math> of <math>L</math> in <math>M</math>;
* a [[Symplectomorphism|diffeomorphism]] <math>f: U_1 \to U_2</math>;

such that <math>f^* \omega_2 = \omega_1</math> and <math>f |_L = \mathrm{id}_L</math>.</blockquote>This statement is proved using the Darboux-Moser-Weinstein theorem, taking <math>X = L</math> a Lagrangian submanifold, together with a version of the [[Whitney extension theorem|Whitney Extension Theorem]] for smooth manifolds.<ref name=":0" />

=== Generalisation: Coisotropic Embedding Theorem ===
Weinstein's result can be generalised by weakening the assumption that <math>L</math> is Lagrangian.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Gotay |first=Mark J. |date=1982 |title=On coisotropic imbeddings of presymplectic manifolds |url=https://www.ams.org/proc/1982-084-01/S0002-9939-1982-0633290-X/ |journal=[[Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society]] |language=en |volume=84 |issue=1 |pages=111–114 |doi=10.1090/S0002-9939-1982-0633290-X |issn=0002-9939 |doi-access=free|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Weinstein |first=Alan |author-link=Alan Weinstein |date=1981-01-01 |title=Neighborhood classification of isotropic embeddings |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/journal-of-differential-geometry/volume-16/issue-1/Neighborhood-classification-of-isotropic-embeddings/10.4310/jdg/1214435995.full |journal=[[Journal of Differential Geometry]] |volume=16 |issue=1 |doi=10.4310/jdg/1214435995 |issn=0022-040X |doi-access=free}}</ref><blockquote>Let <math>M</math> be a [[Differentiable manifold|smooth manifold]] of dimension <math>2n</math>, and <math>\omega_1</math> and <math>\omega_2</math> two symplectic forms on <math>M</math>. Consider a [[Compact space|compact]] submanifold <math>i: L \hookrightarrow M</math> of dimension <math>k</math> which is a [[Isotropic submanifold|coisotropic submanifold]] of both <math>(M,\omega_1)</math> and <math>(M, \omega_2)</math>, and such that <math>i^* \omega_1 = i^* \omega_2</math>. Then there exist

* two open [[Neighbourhood (mathematics)|neighbourhoods]] <math>U_1</math> and <math>U_2</math> of <math>L</math> in <math>M</math>;
* a [[Symplectomorphism|diffeomorphism]] <math>f: U_1 \to U_2</math>;

such that <math>f^* \omega_2 = \omega_1</math> and <math>f |_L = \mathrm{id}_L</math>.</blockquote>

== Weinstein's tubular neighbourhood theorem ==
While [[Darboux's theorem]] identifies locally a symplectic manifold <math>M</math> with <math>T^*L</math>, Weinstein's theorem identifies locally a Lagrangian <math>L</math> with the zero section of <math>T^*L</math>. More precisely<blockquote>Let <math>(M,\omega)</math> be a [[symplectic manifold]] and <math>L</math> a [[Lagrangian submanifold]]. Then there exist

* an open [[Neighbourhood (mathematics)|neighbourhood]] <math>U</math> of <math>L</math> in <math>M</math>;
* an open neighbourhood <math>V</math> of the [[zero section]] <math>L_0</math> in the [[cotangent bundle]] <math>T^*L</math>;
* a [[symplectomorphism]] <math>f: U \to V</math>;

such that <math>f</math> sends <math>L</math> to <math>L_0</math>.</blockquote>

=== Proof ===
This statement relies on the Weinstein's Lagrangian neighbourhood theorem, as well as on the standard [[Tubular neighborhood|tubular neighbourhood]] theorem.<ref name=":0" />
